body.x: LEDDITS Co., Ltd., led by CEO Jaeyong Shim, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Incheon Technopark pavilion, to present VIIK, a handheld 3D scanner that runs AI on the device.

Conventional 3D scanners focus on capturing shape and color. VIIK also generates the type and location of each object during the scan: it builds a real-time color point cloud from LiDAR and an RGB camera and links the AI's object-recognition results to 3D spatial coordinates. Inference runs on NVIDIA Jetson hardware, and per-object segmentation results and center coordinates can be marked in the spatial data. LEDDITS is also developing web-based visualization and sharing so that information gathered on site can be used by other users.

Founded in January 2021, LEDDITS specializes in vision AI and IoT. It develops AI-based video analysis, intelligent industrial monitoring and 3D spatial data processing for manufacturing, shipbuilding and public safety. Its core technologies are deep-learning object recognition, LiDAR-camera sensor fusion, SLAM-based 3D mapping and NVIDIA edge computing, and the company is working to commercialize on-device spatial intelligence that connects spatial data from industrial sites with AI analysis.

LEDDITS reported 2025 revenue of KRW 378.24 million and cumulative revenue of about KRW 996.18 million from 2021 to 2025. It has completed about 50 vision AI and IoT development projects and holds four patent applications and two registered patents. In 2026, it was selected for nine government and public-sector support programs, including the NVIDIA NGG program and the Incheon Startup Park TRYOUT public demonstration project. Its project record includes a license plate recognition system developed with a partner and a demonstration of an IoT sensor-based wildfire monitoring and 3D control system.

Using the NVIDIA Inception network, the company has widened its contacts with global technology companies and investors. In 2026, it took part in NVIDIA AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA Inception Grand Finale and Nautilus x SparkLabs Taiwan. Its main target countries are the United States, Taiwan and Japan. In the United States, LEDDITS plans to test demand in industrial 3D scanning and spatial AI and to look for technology cooperation and investment. In Taiwan, it will pursue field demonstrations and supply chain cooperation centered on semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, and in Japan it is seeking entry through manufacturing equipment management and industrial automation. The company wants partners among industrial 3D scanner distributors, system integrators (SIs) for digital twins and smart factories, and robotics and spatial AI solution companies, with cooperation ranging from local proof-of-concept (PoC) projects to product supply and SDK-based technology partnerships.

LEDDITS aims to start mass production of VIIK by the end of 2026 and to concentrate on field use cases and sales growth in 2027, beginning with manufacturing, shipbuilding and construction before moving into facility management, public safety and robotics. Its business model starts with hardware sales and extends to industry-specific AI models and SDK licenses, VIIK Studio 3D spatial data management software, and a marketplace for sharing and trading data and AI models. The company names stable mass production, overseas certification and field validation, and building an initial sales network as its main challenges. Industrial equipment needs country-specific certification, field performance checks and after-sales support, so early overseas entry takes considerable cost and time. LEDDITS is seeking support for certification and testing costs, introductions to local companies that need demonstrations, and help with overseas distribution and investment.

AVING News, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING News has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING News will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING News will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING News will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.

After CES 2027 concludes, AVING News will co-host a post-show conference with participating companies to highlight their achievements, strengthen their domestic visibility and enhance their corporate reputation.
